title: How a call travels through the layers
intro: Three paths through qa-template, one step at a time. The dot is the call moving between components. Press Play, or step through manually (arrow keys work too).

flows.label: UI test
flows.summary: What happens between a spec asking for dynamicPage and a click landing in the browser.

steps.title: The test asks for dynamicPage
steps.text: The spec never builds anything itself. It names the fixture it needs, and Playwright works out how to create it.
steps.code: test('adds a product to the cart', async ({ dynamicPage }) => {

steps.title: The client's fixtures extend the core
steps.text: Specs import test from their client's fixtures.ts. That file extends the core test instead of replacing it, so every core fixture is available, plus the client's own additions.

steps.title: Playwright resolves the fixture chain
steps.text: dynamicPage declares its dependencies in its signature: page, client, logger and sharedData. Playwright builds each one on demand, so a test that never asks for dynamicPage never pays for it.
steps.code: dynamicPage: async ({ page, client, logger, sharedData }, use) =>

steps.title: The core loads the active client
steps.text: The client fixture calls loadClient(), which reads the CLIENT environment variable and requires clients/<name>/client.ts. This is the only dynamic link between core and client.

steps.title: client.ts hands over its definition
steps.text: The ClientDefinition tells the engine everything app-specific: base URLs per environment, the page registry, the auth strategy and how to build the API client.
steps.code: pages: { login: loginPage, products: productsPage, productDetail: productDetailPage, cart: cartPage },

steps.title: A DynamicPage is built for this test
steps.text: Each test gets its own DynamicPage, bound to its own page, logger and shared data. Nothing is shared between tests running in parallel.

steps.title: goto() loads the page config
steps.text: goto('products') looks the name up in client.pages and calls the config factory with the current page. On the first call it runs onPageInit, then resolves the URL against baseUrl and navigates with retry.

steps.title: executeSection reads the fields
steps.text: The test passes a section name and data. The engine walks the keys of the data, in the test's order, and finds each field's locator and action list in the config.

steps.title: Each action runs by name
steps.text: Action names map to functions: built-in ones (fill, click, check, selectOption and more) merged with any the client registers. An unknown name fails with the section and field in the message.

steps.title: Playwright acts in the browser
steps.text: InputActions and ElementActions call Playwright's auto-waiting locators and log every step; fill also confirms the value landed. That code is written once for every client. The test reads like a description of intent; the engine does the work.

flows.label: API test
flows.summary: How an API spec reaches the server without opening a browser, and what gets retried.

steps.title: The test asks for api
steps.text: API specs request the typed api fixture and never touch page. The api project in playwright.config.ts has no setup dependency and no browser state.
steps.code: test('rejects login for an unknown user', async ({ api }) => {

steps.title: The client narrows the type
steps.text: The client fixture does not build its own API client. It takes the one the core built and narrows it with instanceof, so a wrong CLIENT fails loudly instead of being hidden by a cast.

steps.title: The core builds it from the definition
steps.text: apiClient calls the client's createApiClient. One place decides how the API client is constructed.

steps.title: The test calls an endpoint
steps.text: Endpoint methods are thin. With expectError the call returns the status and body instead of throwing, which is what a negative test needs.
steps.code: await api.post('/users/login', { email, password }, { expectError: true });

steps.title: BaseApiClient sends the request
steps.text: axios is configured from the ClientDefinition: base URL per environment and default headers. Every request is logged as a curl command, with authorization and token headers masked.

steps.title: Only server errors are retried
steps.text: 5xx responses and connection resets are retried up to 3 times, waiting 2, 4 and 8 seconds. A 4xx is never retried: it is an answer, not an outage. With expectError, no status counts as an error, so nothing reaches the retry interceptor.

steps.title: The server answers 401
steps.text: The unknown user is rejected and the test asserts the status. It uses an email that doesn't exist on purpose: repeated wrong passwords lock a real account.

flows.label: Log in once
flows.summary: How the run logs in a single time, and why every UI test starts already signed in.

steps.title: The ui project depends on setup
steps.text: Playwright runs the setup project first, once per run. The api project has no such dependency, so API tests never wait for a login.

steps.title: Setup checks for an auth strategy
steps.text: The setup file is generic. A client without auth is skipped, and its UI tests simply run without saved state.
steps.code: if (!auth) { return setup.skip(true, `Client "${client.name}" has no auth strategy`); }

steps.title: client.auth is the strategy
steps.text: The strategy gets a getter, not the client object, because the object doesn't exist yet while it's being defined.

steps.title: login() uses the same engine as the tests
steps.text: AuthStrategy has two methods: login and isLoggedIn. The implementation builds a DynamicPage, so login has no locators of its own.
steps.code: const dynamicPage = new DynamicPage(page, this.getClient(), new Logger('auth'), new SharedData());

steps.title: The login config fills the form
steps.text: Credentials come from the environment file or CI secrets, never from the code.
steps.code: await dynamicPage.executeSection('form', { email, password, submit: true });

steps.title: Setup waits until the app agrees
steps.text: Instead of a fixed wait, setup polls isLoggedIn until the app shows a signed-in state.

steps.title: The session is saved once
steps.text: Cookies and local storage are written to .auth/<client>.json.

steps.title: Every UI test starts signed in
steps.text: The ui project loads the saved state into each new browser context. One login per run, however many UI tests there are.
